commentary:
Energy is the morning's talking point, and it's a distillate story more than a crude one: gasoil is up 4.4%, heating oil 2.1% and TTF gas 3.4% — helped by Berlin instructing state-owned SEFE to inject gas into storage ahead of winter — dragging WTI up 1.5% to $90.69 and Brent through $103 into today's November expiry. But look under the hood and the crude complex is telling a softer story: Middle East flows are returning toward pre-war levels according to JPMorgan and Goldman estimates, Iraq is discounting October barrels by as much as $37, API reported a 1M-bbl crude build, and Brent puts have outpaced calls for the longest run since June while prompt spreads sit at multi-week lows.

Backwardation is fading — the products squeeze is doing the heavy lifting, not the geopolitical premium. The macro backdrop is all about inflation. Treasuries and bond futures firmed ahead of today's key US inflation print that could reset Fed pricing, with the long bond +0.3% even as 30-year mortgage rates hit 7.3%, the highest since late 2023. Europe cuts the other way: Italian harmonized CPI surprised at 4.1% versus 3.7% expected, part of a broader eurozone inflation jump that pressures the ECB toward tightening — one to watch for Euribor and Bund shorts.

Equity index futures are flat-to-lower ahead of Micron's results, the next read on the AI trade underpinning the Nasdaq. Elsewhere, softs are on fire — arabica +3.1% near records amid a US-Colombia tariff spat according to reports, robusta +3.7%, OJ +3% — while gold's grind to $4,212 and platinum's 1.7% pop reflect the same inflation-hedge bid supporting bonds' rivals.
